parts.text: In this experiment, you will determine the weight of a metre rule using a balancing method. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 1.1. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Place the metre rule on the pivot. Place the load P on the metre rule at the 90.0 cm mark. Keeping P at the 90.0 cm mark, adjust the position of the metre rule on the pivot so that the metre rule is as near as possible to being balanced.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Write down the reading on the metre rule at the position of the pivot. The pivot is at the .................... cm mark of the metre rule.

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Determine the weight W of the metre rule using the equation W = Px y , where P = 2.0 N. P is the weight of load P . W = ...........................................................[1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Keep the pivot at the same position, as recorded in (a)(i) . Move load P to the 95.0 cm mark. Place the load Q on the metre rule and adjust its position so that the rule balances.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) On Fig. 1.2 mark, with a letter X, the approximate position of Q . [1] Fig. 1.2

parts.label: vi
parts.text: (vi) Calculate the product bQ , where Q = 1.0 N. Q is the weight of load Q . bQ = ...............................................................

parts.label: vii
parts.text: (vii) Calculate the product cW , using the value of W determined in part (a)(iv) . cW = ............................................................... [2]
